sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized IFA (peripheral staining pattern); no functional assay of the tagged construct reported. L5 reports WT FLAG-EphA2 surface expression is detectable; a point-mutant variant (M3) shows reduced surface expression, but this reflects the mutation, not the tag.
sites.rationale: EphA2 is a type I single-pass transmembrane receptor with signal peptide spanning residues 1–23 (landmarks, authoritative). The mature N-terminus begins at residue 24 (A), so an N-terminal tag on the extracellular face must be inserted after residue 23 (A). Python verification confirms seq[23]=A and seq[24]=A. Because the paper names no residue number but EphA2 has exactly one extracellular terminus, the position is topology_derived and uniquely determined. The tag is >500 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 541), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance constraint. Full-length EphA2 constructs (NM_004431.5) were engineered with an N-terminal HA-tag and expressed in mammalian cells. Non-permeabilized immunofluorescence assays confirmed a peripheral (plasma-membrane) staining pattern for all six constructs, establishing that the HA-tag is displayed on the extracellular face. L4/L5 (PMC8254660) independently confirm a FLAG-tagged full-length EphA2 whose FLAG epitope is detected on the cell surface by anti-FLAG antibody, consistent with the same N-terminal extracellular position.

sources.claim: Immuno-fluorescence assays (IFAs) against the extracellular HA-tag performed without cell-permeabilization showed a peripheral pattern of protein expression for all constructs, confirming their presence on the plasma membrane (Fig. 2 b).

literature_notes: L1–L3 (PMC9746569) and L4–L5 (PMC8254660) both support the same junction (after residue 23, the signal-peptide cleavage site) via different tags (HA and FLAG respectively). Because both papers pin the identical junction on the identical protein, this is one site, not two; L3 is used as the primary clip (strongest surface evidence). No ledger line supports any internal loop insertion in EphA2. L4 mentions EGFP co-tagging; EGFP on a type I TM protein is almost certainly C-terminal (intracellular) and is not proposed as a surface site because no ledger line confirms extracellular EGFP display, and the C-terminus of EphA2 is intracellular (residues 559–976). L5 notes that the M3 point-mutant shows reduced surface FLAG signal, but this reflects the mutant's trafficking defect, not a tag-position effect; no other_position entry is warranted because the paper does not report the M3 mutation as a tag-insertion site.
